```{r, knitr, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE,
                      fig.align="center", comment="#>")

pkgs=c("FLCore", "FLBRP", "FLRebuild", "icesdata", "spict", "ggplot2", "ggplotFL")
ok  =all(vapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly=TRUE))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval=ok)
```

# Introduction

SPiCT (Pedersen and Berg, 2017) provides base graphics plots
(`plot.spictcls`, `plotspict.*`). This vignette shows the equivalent plots
built with `ggplot2` and `ggplotFL`, in the same style as the diagnostics
used for the other assessment models (time series with confidence
intervals, Kobe phase plots, production functions, runs tests on residuals,
retrospective and hindcast cross-validation, and priors against
posteriors).

The `plotSpict*` functions are thin wrappers: the fit is converted to the
method-agnostic `cmpAssess` summary with `spict2cmp` (which uses only the
exported SPiCT API) and plotted with the generic `cmp*` functions, which can
also overlay other assessment methods (see the `assessment-comparison`
vignette).

The example is North Sea plaice, fitted as in the `spict` vignette, with
priors for $r$, $K$, $n$ and the initial depletion derived from the
`FLBRP` reference points and exploitable biomass as the index.

```{r, pkgs}
library(FLCore)
library(FLBRP)
library(ggplotFL)
library(ggplot2)
library(spict)

library(mpb)
```

# Fit

```{r, fit}
data(icesdata, package="icesdata")
stk=window(icesdata[["ple.27.420"]], end=2020)

eq =FLRebuild::eql(stk, model="bevholtSV")
rf =FLRebuild::refptsEB(eq)
pt =FLRebuild::pellatParams(FLPar(msy =rf["msy",   "yield"],
                                  bmsy=rf["msy",   "eb"],
                                  k   =rf["virgin","eb"]))
idx=FLRebuild::ebiomass(stk)
psi=c(idx[, 1])/c(pt["k"])

cv2sd=function(x) sqrt(log(1+x^2))
scale=1000
yrs  =an(dimnames(catch(stk))$year)

inp=list(obsC=c(catch(stk))/scale, timeC=yrs,
         obsI=c(idx)/scale,        timeI=yrs,
         dteuler=1/4)
inp$priors=list(
  logr     =c(log(c(pt["r"])),       cv2sd(0.3), 1),
  logK     =c(log(c(pt["k"])/scale), cv2sd(0.5), 1),
  logn     =c(log(c(pt["p"])+1),     cv2sd(0.3), 1),
  logbkfrac=c(log(psi),              cv2sd(0.3), 1),
  logsdi   =c(log(0.1),              0.5,        1))
inp=check.inp(inp, verbose=FALSE)

fit=fit.spict(inp)
fit=calc.process.resid(fit)
fit=calc.osa.resid(fit)
fit$opt$convergence
```

The retrospective (`spict::retro`) refits the model to five peels; the
same peels are used for the hindcast.

```{r, retro}
fit=retro(fit, nretroyear=5)
```

# Time series

`spictTS` extracts annual estimates and 95% confidence intervals as a
`data.frame`, and `plotSpictTS` plots them. Dashed lines are the
deterministic reference points ($B_{MSY}$, $F_{MSY}$, MSY); `scale` converts
back to tonnes.

```{r, ts, fig.height=6}
plotSpictTS(fit, scale=scale)
```

The same plot from the common summary, which is what `plotSpictTS` does
internally:

```{r, cmp}
sp=spict2cmp(fit, scale=scale)
sp
```

Stock status relative to MSY reference points.

```{r, status}
plotSpictStatus(fit)
```

## As FLQuants

`spict2FLQuants` converts the fit to `FLQuants`. With `iter` the
uncertainty is represented by log-normal draws, so that `ggplotFL::plot`
shows the median and quantile ribbons as for any other FLR model.

```{r, flq, fig.height=7}
flq=spict2FLQuants(fit, iter=500)
plot(flq)
```

Without `iter` the point estimates can be combined with other `FLQuants`,
e.g. the exploitable biomass from the age-structured assessment.

```{r, flqcmp, fig.height=3}
bsp=FLQuant(c(spict2FLQuants(fit, "B")[["B"]])*scale, dimnames=dimnames(idx))
cmp=FLQuants(SPiCT=bsp, Assessment=idx)

ggplot(cmp, aes(year, data, colour=qname)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x="Year", y="Exploitable biomass (t)", colour=NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Kobe phase plot

The terminal year is shown as a large point with its 95% confidence intervals.

```{r, kobe, fig.height=5.5}
plotSpictKobe(fit)
```

# Production function

The Pella-Tomlinson production function implied by the SPiCT estimates,
with the realised surplus production $B_{t+1}-B_t+C_t$ in each year.

```{r, prod}
plotSpictProduction(fit)
```

# Model fit

Observed (points) and fitted catch and index, with 95% confidence intervals.

```{r, fitted}
plotSpictFit(fit)
```

# Residuals

## One-step-ahead residuals

The 3-sigma band is green if the runs test is passed and red if it fails;
points outside the band are outlined in red.

```{r, runs}
plotSpictRuns(fit)
```

```{r, acf, fig.height=3}
plotSpictACF(fit)
```

```{r, qq, fig.height=3}
plotSpictQQ(fit)
```

## Process residuals

```{r, process}
plotSpictProcess(fit)
```

```{r, processacf, fig.height=3}
plotSpictACF(fit, "process")
```

# Retrospective analysis

```{r, retroplot}
plotSpictRetro(fit)
```

# Hindcast cross-validation

Each peel predicts the index one year ahead as $qB_{T+1}$, where $T$ is the
peel's last year; MASE is calculated by `cmpMASE` from these predictions.
Unlike `spict::hindcast`, catches are also removed from the peeled years.

```{r, hindcast, fig.height=4}
plotSpictHindcast(fit)
```

# Priors and posteriors

```{r, priors, fig.height=5}
plotSpictPriors(fit)
```

# References

Pedersen, M.W. and Berg, C.W. (2017). A stochastic surplus production model
in continuous time. *Fish and Fisheries*, 18(2), 226-243.
